title: Release 2.1
content:
The Apache Paimon community is pleased to announce Apache Paimon 2.1.0 and PyPaimon 2.1.0. This release builds on Paimon's multimodal lakehouse capabilities with expanded Python-native execution, storage and merge correctness fixes, and improvements to distributed data processing.

These notes describe the code in the approved 2.1.0 release. See the complete changelog for all changes since 2.0.0.

PyPaimon and Native Execution

PyPaimon expands its optional Rust-backed execution through pypaimon-rust, including scan planning, Arrow reads and writes, table updates and upserts, and native commit paths for supported tables and catalogs.

The release extends native support for nested Data Evolution rows, BLOB collections, Variant updates, column-subset writes, external data paths, dynamic buckets, and branch writes. Resolved REST metadata can be reused by native readers, avoiding repeated catalog setup in parallel reads.

Native execution remains capability-dependent. Follow the PyPaimon documentation for options, optional dependencies and supported combinations, rather than assuming every table or storage backend follows the same execution path.

Correctness and Reliability

Important fixes include:

  • Snapshot expiration rejects invalid retain_min values rather than deleting files belonging to retained snapshots.
  • Projected and partial-update reads preserve sequence-group deletion state.
  • OSS retry handling covers QpsLimitExceeded and server-side errors, including responses whose error bodies cannot be parsed.
  • Native planning and reading better preserve Java-compatible scan semantics, row tracking, deletion vectors and BLOB limits.

The release also improves Ray-based processing, including distributed BLOB read request locality and native primary-key scan sharding.

Engine Artifacts and Upgrade Checks

Convenience artifacts include connectors for Flink 1.x and 2.x, Spark 3.x and 4.x, Hive, and supported object-storage filesystems. Choose the artifact for your exact engine version; Spark artifact names also include the Scala binary version, such as paimon-spark-3.5_2.12 or paimon-spark-4.1_2.13.

Before upgrading, test your table types, merge engines, catalog and filesystem configuration against the released version. Review the 2.1 documentation for compatibility and installation requirements.

Downloads and Packages

  • Apache Paimon 2.1.0 source, signature and SHA-512 checksum
  • PyPaimon 2.1.0 source, signature and SHA-512 checksum
  • Apache Paimon KEYS for signature verification
  • Apache Paimon 2.1.0 GitHub release
  • PyPaimon 2.1.0 on PyPI
  • Apache Paimon 2.1 documentation

Install the Python convenience package with:

pip install pypaimon==2.1.0

Thank you to every contributor, reviewer and user who helped develop and verify this release.
